**TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT**

FitFix Technical Requirements Document

_Implementation design for the reactive equipment maintenance MVP_

Version 1.0 | Approved technical design | 21 September 2026

| **Decision summary**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Build FitFix as a modular full-stack Next.js application backed by Neon PostgreSQL and Prisma. Clerk provides identity and one-gym organization membership, Cloudinary stores fault evidence, Resend delivers transactional email, and Vercel hosts the application. Tenant isolation, explicit lifecycle transitions, durable audit history, optimistic concurrency and an email outbox are mandatory controls. |

# Purpose of this document

This TRD converts the approved FitFix Product Requirements Document into an implementation-ready design for Allen, the solo developer and product owner. It defines component boundaries, data structures, API contracts, security controls, failure handling, tests, deployment order and rollback steps. The design covers the approved reactive-maintenance MVP and deliberately excludes preventive maintenance, member reporting, multiple locations, technician accounts, inventory, billing and AI features.

# 2 Executive technical summary

FitFix will use a modular monolith: one Next.js codebase contains the responsive interface, server-rendered pages, Route Handlers and domain services. This shape matches the ten-week solo delivery constraint and avoids a second deployable backend. Domain modules keep authorization, validation and lifecycle logic separate from route files, so a later service split remains possible without designing for it now.

PostgreSQL is the operational source of truth because the product depends on tenant-scoped relationships, assignments, immutable history, costs and multi-record transactions. Every tenant-owned record carries a gym identifier. Route handlers derive the current gym from the authenticated session and never accept a caller-supplied gym identifier as authority.

The design is implementation ready. Remaining questions concern commercial launch rather than MVP construction: legal retention policy, product-name availability, operator validation and final provider-plan selection. These items remain visible in the risk register and release gates.

## Architecture decisions

| **ID** | **Decision**                              | **Rationale**                                                            | **Consequence**                                                        |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ADR-01 | Next.js modular monolith                  | Lowest delivery and operational overhead for one developer.              | No independent API deployment in the MVP.                              |
| ADR-02 | Neon PostgreSQL and Prisma                | Relational integrity and transactions suit the workflow.                 | Schema changes require reviewed migrations.                            |
| ADR-03 | Clerk Organizations                       | Managed identity, invitations and roles align with gym workspaces.       | Clerk webhook reconciliation and vendor exit mapping are required.     |
| ADR-04 | One gym per user                          | Approved MVP rule removes workspace switching.                           | A future release must remove the unique membership constraint.         |
| ADR-05 | Purpose-specific transition endpoints     | Prevents invalid generic status updates.                                 | More endpoints, clearer authorization and audit behavior.              |
| ADR-06 | Database email outbox plus immediate send | Normal email target is under one minute without blocking user responses. | Failure recovery is eventual rather than guaranteed within one minute. |
| ADR-07 | No shared cache initially                 | Indexed database queries meet approved scale.                            | Add cache only after measurement identifies a bottleneck.              |

# 3 Source PRD and scope

The source of product scope is FitFix Product Requirements Document version 1.0, approved on 21 September 2026. The technical design preserves its terminology and requirement identifiers FR-01 through FR-20 and NFR-01 through NFR-15.

## Confirmed MVP scope

- One responsive gym workspace per tenant with manager and staff accounts.
- Equipment registry, archive behavior, equipment QR labels and searchable equipment selection.
- Reactive fault reporting with severity, equipment availability, discovery time, immediate action and up to five photos.
- Manager review, internal or external assignment, target date, comments, resolution, verification, closure and reopening.
- Equipment history, downtime intervals, costs, search, filters, in-app notifications, email and manager analytics.
- Saved fault-report drafts containing fields and photos for 30 days after the most recent save.

## Approved assumptions and constraints

| **ID** | **Assumption or constraint**                          | **Technical effect**                                                          |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A-01   | A user belongs to one gym in the MVP.                 | Unique active membership by user; no organization switcher.                   |
| A-02   | A gym represents one physical location.               | Timezone and currency are stored at gym level.                                |
| A-03   | External technicians do not sign in.                  | They are tenant-owned records referenced by assignments.                      |
| A-04   | Connectivity is required.                             | No offline queue; forms preserve safe local state during recoverable errors.  |
| A-05   | Staff cannot edit original evidence after submission. | Corrections use chronological updates; managers may revise controlled fields. |
| A-06   | New reports may be incomplete for assignment.         | They show Needs triage, Unassigned and Not set until manager review.          |
| A-07   | Portfolio MVP has no billing or commercial SLA.       | Usage limits are monitored; legal and commercial review remain launch gates.  |

## Out of scope

- Preventive maintenance and inspections.
- Member-submitted reports.
- Multiple locations per gym.
- Authenticated technician portal.
- Parts inventory and procurement.
- Subscription billing and plan enforcement.
- Browser push notifications and AI diagnosis.
- Profile and notification preferences beyond provider-managed account settings.

# 5 User technical profile and learning assessment

Allen confirmed no material change to the baseline profile. The design therefore uses familiar technologies where they fit and isolates unfamiliar production concerns into timeboxed spikes.

| **Capability or technology**             | **Classification**  | **Why needed**                                      | **Learning or verification**                              | **Alternative and consequence**                                 |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Next.js, React and TypeScript            | Known               | UI and server application                           | App Router boundaries and server-only imports             | Separate API adds deployment and coordination overhead.         |
| Neon PostgreSQL and Prisma               | Known               | Relational operational data                         | Migration and pooled connection configuration             | MongoDB reduces relational constraints and transaction clarity. |
| Clerk and Organizations                  | Known plus adjacent | Identity, invitations and membership                | Webhook verification and session-based tenant resolution  | Custom invitations increase security-sensitive code.            |
| Cloudinary signed uploads                | Known plus adjacent | Draft and submitted evidence                        | Signature constraints, deletion and orphan cleanup        | Server proxy uploads increase function time and bandwidth.      |
| Transactions and optimistic concurrency  | Adjacent            | Atomic history and safe simultaneous edits          | Interactive transactions, version checks and 409 handling | Last-write-wins risks silent data loss.                         |
| Email outbox and after                   | Adjacent            | Fast normal delivery with recoverable failure state | Idempotency keys and reconciliation                       | Synchronous-only email can lose committed notifications.        |
| Playwright and security matrix           | Adjacent            | Critical lifecycle and tenant tests                 | Fixtures, role sessions and accessible locators           | Manual-only testing is not repeatable.                          |
| Tenant isolation and production recovery | New or high-risk    | Primary privacy and operational controls            | Negative authorization tests and restore rehearsal        | No credible simpler alternative for a multi-tenant product.     |

## Technical spikes

| **ID** | **Question**                                                       | **Timebox** | **Required output**                        | **Success criterion**                                                |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SP-01  | Can tenant guards prevent every cross-gym read and write path?     | 4 hours     | Automated permission matrix                | All altered IDs return 404 or 403 with no data leakage.              |
| SP-02  | Do Clerk membership events reconcile safely?                       | 4 hours     | Verified webhook prototype and replay test | Duplicates are harmless; missed events can be reconciled.            |
| SP-03  | Can lifecycle writes remain atomic under concurrency?              | 4 hours     | Transaction and stale-version test         | One write succeeds; stale write returns 409 without partial history. |
| SP-04  | Can normal email submit within 60 seconds?                         | 3 hours     | Outbox and Resend prototype                | Provider accepts one message and records one provider ID.            |
| SP-05  | Can draft photos expire without deleting submitted evidence?       | 3 hours     | Cleanup test with mixed media states       | Only expired DRAFT assets move to DELETE_PENDING and delete.         |
| SP-06  | Can production data be restored within the selected provider plan? | 3 hours     | Documented backup and restore rehearsal    | Restore meets the approved recovery procedure before launch.         |

# 6 Technical capability breakdown

| **Area**       | **Capabilities**                                                                 | **Dependencies**                                    | **Primary failure treatment**                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend       | Responsive navigation, forms, autosave, timelines, dashboards, accessible states | Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, accessible primitives | Preserve input, focus first error, retry without duplication.     |
| Backend        | Tenant context, authorization, validation, transition services, query services   | Route Handlers, Zod, Prisma                         | Typed errors, transactions and idempotency keys.                  |
| Data           | Relational entities, unique constraints, status intervals, audit and outbox      | Neon PostgreSQL, Prisma Migrate                     | Expand-contract migrations and reconciliation queries.            |
| Identity       | Sign-up, session, organization, invite and deactivation                          | Clerk Organizations and verified webhooks           | Session remains authority; webhook replay repairs local mirror.   |
| Media          | Signed upload, validation, draft attachment and cleanup                          | Cloudinary                                          | Preserve report fields and mark failed media for retry.           |
| Email          | Templates, dispatch and delivery tracking                                        | Resend, React Email, Next.js after                  | Outbox retains failures; safe later retry.                        |
| Infrastructure | Preview, staging, production and environment configuration                       | GitHub and Vercel                                   | Protected secrets, deployment gates and instant app rollback.     |
| Operations     | Structured logs, metrics, alerts and runbooks                                    | Vercel logs and Sentry or equivalent                | Correlate request, actor, gym and entity without logging content. |

# 7 Architecture

![Figure 1  FitFix system component architecture](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 1 FitFix system component architecture_

## Component responsibilities

| **Component**                | **Responsibilities**                                                          | **Boundary**                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Next.js pages and components | Render public, shared and manager-only experiences.                           | No direct database or secret access from client components. |
| Route Handlers               | Parse requests, authenticate, validate and translate service results to HTTP. | Do not contain domain transition logic.                     |
| Domain services              | Enforce permissions, workflow rules, transactions and audit writes.           | Receive a trusted tenant context rather than raw gym IDs.   |
| Query services               | Build tenant-scoped lists, history and dashboard aggregates.                  | Read-only; no hidden state mutation.                        |
| Prisma data layer            | Typed persistence, constraints and migrations.                                | All tenant-owned queries include gymId.                     |
| Integration adapters         | Clerk, Cloudinary and Resend API calls.                                       | Vendor payloads are converted to internal types.            |

## Primary write flow

![Figure 2  Fault submission and notification sequence](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 2 Fault submission and notification sequence_

The database transaction creates the fault, applies a permitted equipment-status change, attaches draft media, records audit history, creates in-app notifications and writes the email outbox entry. External email delivery occurs after commit. A Cloudinary or email failure therefore cannot roll back a committed fault or leave its core history incomplete.

# 8 Application and repository design

The repository groups code by business capability. Route files remain thin and call server-only services. Shared UI contains presentation primitives rather than maintenance rules.

| **Path**                   | **Responsibility**                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| src/app/(public)           | Landing, privacy, terms and support pages.                                 |
| src/app/(auth)             | Clerk sign-in and sign-up routes.                                          |
| src/app/(workspace)        | Authenticated layouts, dashboard, equipment, faults and notifications.     |
| src/app/(manager)          | Staff, analytics and gym settings guarded by manager policy.               |
| src/app/api                | Route Handlers, Clerk webhook, upload signature and operational endpoints. |
| src/features/auth          | Tenant context, role policies and membership reconciliation.               |
| src/features/equipment     | Equipment commands, queries, QR generation and status intervals.           |
| src/features/faults        | Drafts, reports, assignments, lifecycle and timeline.                      |
| src/features/notifications | In-app notifications, email templates and outbox processor.                |
| src/features/dashboard     | Role-specific aggregate queries and response models.                       |
| src/lib/db                 | Single Prisma client, transaction helpers and pagination.                  |
| src/lib/integrations       | Clerk, Cloudinary and Resend adapters.                                     |
| src/lib/validation         | Shared Zod schemas and error mapping.                                      |
| prisma/schema.prisma       | Database models, enums, relations, constraints and indexes.                |
| prisma/migrations          | Reviewed, ordered schema migrations.                                       |
| tests                      | Unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, security and load tests.          |

## Configuration

- Validate environment variables at application startup and fail closed when a required secret is missing.
- Keep server-only configuration outside modules imported by client components.
- Use separate Clerk, Neon, Cloudinary and Resend environments or credentials for development, staging and production.
- Do not store secrets, provider payloads, production exports or user evidence in Git.

# 9 Data design

![Figure 3  Core FitFix entity relationships](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 3 Core FitFix entity relationships_

## Data conventions

- Use UUID primary keys internally and opaque public identifiers in URLs and QR codes.
- Store timestamps in UTC as timezone-aware PostgreSQL values and present them using Gym.timeZone.
- Store money as Decimal(12,2) with Gym.currencyCode; never use floating-point values for cost.
- Use archivedAt or deactivatedAt for operational deletion. Historical faults, updates and audit events are not cascaded away.
- Add version integers to mutable workflow records and increment them on every accepted update.

| name                    | String(120) | Yes          | None        | Trimmed                 |
| slug                    | String(80)  | Yes          | None        | Unique                  |

## Lifecycle constraints

| **Rule**                    | **Constraint**                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Assignment exclusivity      | Exactly one of assigneeMemberId or externalTechnicianId is present after ASSIGNED.          |
| Assignment completeness     | Target date is required when entering ASSIGNED.                                             |
| Resolution completeness     | Resolution summary is required when entering RESOLVED.                                      |
| Closure authority           | Only a manager may enter CLOSED or reopen a closed report.                                  |
| Reporter edits              | Submitted original evidence is immutable to staff. Corrections use FaultUpdate.             |
| Equipment return to service | A manager confirms AVAILABLE during review or closure.                                      |
| Tenant integrity            | Referenced equipment, members and technicians must share the fault gymId.                   |
| Draft conversion            | A draft becomes a fault once; repeated submit with the same key returns the existing fault. |

## Migration strategy

- Use additive expand migrations first: create nullable columns, new tables and indexes without removing existing fields.
- Deploy code that can read both old and new shapes, backfill in bounded batches, then enforce constraints in a later migration.
- Do not combine destructive schema changes with the release that first stops using the old field.
- Test every migration against an empty database and a production-shaped seeded database. Record duration and lock behavior.
- Create a verified backup or branch before production migration and record the exact application commit and migration name.

## Request and response conventions

- Validate path, query and body input with shared schemas. Reject unknown fields on mutation endpoints.
- Return application errors as { code, message, fieldErrors?, requestId }. Do not expose stack traces, SQL, provider payloads or cross-tenant existence.
- Require an Idempotency-Key header for fault submission, invitations and transition endpoints that trigger notifications.
- Require the client version on mutable workflow requests. A stale version returns 409 with the current safe summary.
- Use 404 rather than revealing that a resource exists in another gym. Use 403 only when the resource is known within the caller's gym but the action is forbidden.
- Allow sort and filter values only from documented fields. Parameterize all database access through Prisma.

## Representative fault submission contract

| **Element** | **Definition**                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Request     | POST /api/faults with Idempotency-Key header.                                                                                              |
| Body        | draftId?, equipmentPublicId, title, description, severity, equipmentStatus, discoveredAt, immediateAction?, mediaAssetIds\[\], version?    |
| Validation  | Required text lengths; valid enum values; equipment and media belong to caller gym; at most five attached photos; discovery time is valid. |
| Transaction | Create fault, apply permitted equipment status, attach media, write timeline and audit, create notifications and outbox.                   |
| Success     | 201 with reference, status REPORTED, triageState NEEDS_TRIAGE, version and permitted actions.                                              |
| Duplicate   | Same idempotency key and canonical request returns the prior success. Different body with reused key returns 409.                          |
| Failure     | 400 validation; 401 unauthenticated; 403 inactive member; 404 unknown tenant resource; 409 stale or duplicate conflict; 429 rate limited.  |

## Integration boundaries

| **Integration** | **Secrets and trust**                                                       | **Timeout and retry**                                                          | **Verification and exit**                                                                      |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Clerk           | Publishable key client-side; secret and webhook signing secret server-side. | Backend calls use bounded timeout; webhook provider retry plus reconciliation. | Verify signatures and event IDs. Store Clerk IDs so identity can be remapped during migration. |
| Cloudinary      | API secret server-side only; client receives constrained signature.         | Direct upload retry is user initiated; deletion retries from DELETE_PENDING.   | Allow formats, size and folder prefix. Store public ID and metadata for export or migration.   |
| Resend          | API key server-side; verified sending domain.                               | Immediate attempt after commit; exponential backoff for retained outbox work.  | Use dedupe key and provider message ID. Email templates remain application-owned.              |
| Vercel          | Deployment credentials and environment variables restricted by environment. | Functions use documented timeouts; scheduler is not the sole source of truth.  | Repository and database remain portable; no Vercel-only data store is required.                |

# 11 Security and privacy

## Authentication and authorization

Clerk authenticates the user and provides the active organization claim. FitFix authorization is separate: each route resolves the local Gym and active GymMember, then calls a policy for the requested action. Client-side hiding improves usability but never grants authority.

| **Action**                                 | **Manager**      | **Staff**                       | **Additional rule**                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| View equipment and active faults           | Allow            | Allow                           | Same gym only.                                                                    |
| Create fault or draft                      | Allow            | Allow                           | Reporter may only reference same-gym equipment.                                   |
| Edit original submitted evidence           | Allow with audit | Deny                            | Staff corrections use updates immediately after submission.                       |
| Review severity and equipment status       | Allow            | Deny                            | Reporter may restrict equipment during initial report but cannot restore service. |
| Assign work and target date                | Allow            | Deny                            | Exactly one internal or external assignee.                                        |
| Add update                                 | Allow            | Allow when reporter or assignee | Same-gym active member.                                                           |
| Mark resolved                              | Allow            | Allow when internal assignee    | Resolution summary required.                                                      |
| Close or reopen                            | Allow            | Deny                            | Reopen reason required.                                                           |
| Manage staff, technicians and gym settings | Allow            | Deny                            | Membership changes are audited.                                                   |

## Security controls

- Tenant isolation: every tenant-owned query includes gymId from trusted server context; negative tests alter every public identifier.
- Least privilege: only manager policies can manage access, assignment, closure, archive, analytics and settings.
- Input safety: schema validation, text-length limits, enum allow lists, safe internal destinations and sanitized filenames.
- Media safety: signed uploads restrict folder, resource type, formats, count and 10 MB size. The Cloudinary secret never reaches the browser.
- CSRF and origin: Clerk session protections remain enabled; mutation requests validate allowed origins where applicable.
- Secrets: use environment-scoped secret storage; rotate after exposure and never include values in logs or client bundles.
- Encryption: HTTPS is required in transit. Managed providers supply encryption at rest; exact plan claims must be verified before commercial launch.
- Logging redaction: exclude descriptions, comments, image URLs, email bodies, session tokens, provider secrets and raw webhook payloads.
- Abuse controls: rate-limit sign-up, invitations, upload signatures, report creation, comments and email-triggering transitions by user and gym.
- Auditability: access, assignment, lifecycle, cost, archive and membership changes create immutable AuditEvent rows.

## Privacy and retention

| **Data class**                         | **MVP retention**                             | **Deletion behavior**                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fault drafts and unattached media      | 30 days after last save                       | Expire draft, mark media DELETE_PENDING and reconcile deletion.               |
| Submitted faults and equipment history | Retained for portfolio MVP                    | Archive rather than delete; commercial policy requires legal review.          |
| Account identity                       | While account is active                       | Clerk deletion deactivates local profile while preserving attributed history. |
| Audit events                           | Retained with operational history             | No user-facing edit or delete endpoint.                                       |
| Email outbox payload                   | Until delivery plus operational review period | Minimize payload; clear or redact content after terminal state.               |

# 12 Reliability and error handling

| **Condition**                      | **System behavior**                                                     | **User-visible result**                                           | **Recovery or monitoring**              |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Invalid input                      | Reject before mutation; return field errors.                            | Focus first invalid field and preserve valid input.               | Correct and retry.                      |
| Unauthenticated or inactive member | Stop before resource lookup.                                            | Sign-in or access-revoked message.                                | Re-authenticate or contact manager.     |
| Cross-tenant identifier            | Return 404 without revealing existence.                                 | Resource not found.                                               | Security event sampled for review.      |
| Stale version                      | Abort transaction with 409.                                             | Explain that the record changed and show safe refresh action.     | Reload and intentionally reapply.       |
| Duplicate submission               | Return original result for the same idempotency key.                    | One confirmation and one fault.                                   | No manual action.                       |
| Database timeout                   | Roll back all writes.                                                   | No success confirmation; form or draft remains available.         | Retry with backoff; alert on threshold. |
| Cloudinary upload failure          | Do not attach failed asset; retain draft fields and successful media.   | Retry photo or continue when permitted.                           | User retry; cleanup orphan metadata.    |
| Email provider failure             | Keep committed fault and in-app notification; retain outbox record.     | Core action succeeds; email is pending.                           | Retry later and alert on backlog.       |
| Clerk webhook failure              | Return non-2xx after safe failure; session remains immediate authority. | No interruption to valid session action.                          | Provider retry and reconciliation.      |
| Rate limit                         | Return 429 with retry guidance.                                         | Wait and retry message.                                           | Monitor repeated abuse patterns.        |
| Unavailable dashboard aggregate    | Fail the affected panel without hiding primary navigation.              | Actionable retry state.                                           | Log query and request ID.               |
| Partial media deletion             | Keep DELETE_PENDING state.                                              | No broken report because attached media is excluded from cleanup. | Idempotent reconciliation.              |

## Concurrency and idempotency

- Use version-based optimistic concurrency for equipment, drafts and fault lifecycle records.
- Write the business record, status interval, timeline, audit event, notification and outbox record in one database transaction.
- Give every side effect a unique dedupe key derived from event type, entity and recipient.
- Claim outbox rows atomically before sending and accept that an external timeout may produce an unknown result. Reconcile by provider message ID and dedupe key.
- Treat webhook and scheduled reconciliation delivery as at least once; store processed event IDs and make handlers safe to replay.

## Recovery objectives

The portfolio MVP has no contractual availability target. Before launch, SP-06 must verify the selected Neon plan's backup and restore capability. The working recovery targets are a maximum 24-hour data loss window and four-hour service restoration, subject to that verification. A commercial release requires tighter, contractually supported targets.

# 13 Performance and scalability

| **Metric**              | **Approved MVP target**                     | **Measurement context**                                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary page load       | Under 3 seconds at p75                      | Mid-range mobile profile, simulated Fast 4G, production build and seeded tenant. |
| API read latency        | Under 500 ms at p95                         | Excludes third-party latency; measured at application boundary.                  |
| API mutation latency    | Under 800 ms at p95                         | Excludes file transfer and post-response email work.                             |
| Normal email submission | Provider accepts within 60 seconds          | Measured from committed triggering action to provider message ID.                |
| Concurrent-use test     | 50 active sessions                          | Representative manager and staff mix.                                            |
| Throughput test         | 20 API requests per second for five minutes | Error rate below 1 percent excluding intentional 4xx tests.                      |
| Tenant data volume      | 500 equipment and 5,000 faults              | Includes updates, notifications and status intervals.                            |
| Evidence upload         | Five images, 10 MB each                     | JPEG, PNG or WebP; direct browser-to-Cloudinary transfer.                        |
| Draft retention         | 30 days after last save                     | Daily cleanup is sufficient for portfolio MVP.                                   |

## Indexes and query strategy

- FaultReport: (gymId, status, severity), (gymId, targetDate), (gymId, equipmentId, createdAt), and (gymId, assigneeMemberId, status).
- Equipment: unique (gymId, assetId), plus (gymId, currentStatus), category and location indexes.
- Notification: (recipientMemberId, readAt, createdAt). EmailOutbox: (status, nextAttemptAt).
- EquipmentStatusInterval: (equipmentId, startedAt) with a constraint or transaction rule allowing one open interval.
- Use bounded date ranges for analytics and cursor pagination for lists. Inspect query plans for dashboard and history fixtures.

## Caching

No shared application cache is required initially. Server-rendered reads query indexed PostgreSQL data, and mutations revalidate the affected Next.js paths. Static public pages may use framework caching. Tenant dashboard responses remain uncached until measurement proves a need because stale urgent or out-of-service data would reduce operational trust.

# 14 Observability and operations

| **Signal**      | **Required fields**                                       | **Alert or review threshold**                                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Request log     | requestId, route, status, duration, actor ID, gym ID      | 5xx rate above 2 percent for five minutes.                          |
| Security denial | requestId, actor ID, gym ID, action, reason code          | Repeated cross-tenant or upload-signature attempts.                 |
| Database        | query class, duration, error code, pool state             | p95 query latency above 300 ms or connection exhaustion.            |
| Outbox          | pending count, oldest age, attempts, terminal failures    | Oldest normal-priority email above 10 minutes or rising backlog.    |
| Webhook         | provider, event type, processing result, age              | Repeated signature failures or unprocessed events above 10 minutes. |
| Media cleanup   | eligible, deleted, failed and oldest pending              | DELETE_PENDING older than 24 hours.                                 |
| Core business   | new faults, unresolved high severity, overdue assignments | Used for operational dashboard, not paging by default.              |

Logs must use structured fields and a shared request ID across route, service and integration layers. Dashboards should separate application health from gym-maintenance analytics. Allen owns MVP incident review, provider-status checks, recovery execution and the post-incident note.

## Operational runbooks

- Authentication incident: confirm Clerk status, reject unverifiable sessions, inspect recent membership events and reconcile after recovery.
- Database incident: stop writes if consistency is uncertain, preserve drafts locally, confirm Neon status and execute the recovery procedure.
- Email backlog: keep in-app notifications available, inspect provider status, pause unsafe retries and reconcile by dedupe key.
- Media incident: disable new upload signatures if validation or account security is uncertain; existing fault pages continue with safe fallbacks.
- Tenant-isolation incident: disable affected route or deployment immediately, preserve evidence, identify exposure scope and do not resume until negative tests pass.

## Test environments and data

- Unit tests use deterministic factories without network access.
- Integration tests use an isolated PostgreSQL database with migrations applied from zero.
- Contract tests use provider test modes or recorded, non-sensitive fixtures and verify webhook signatures.
- End-to-end tests create distinct manager, reporter and assignee identities and never share production credentials.
- The load fixture contains the approved maximum tested tenant volume and representative status distributions.
- CI blocks merge on formatting, type checking, unit tests, integration tests, migration validation and critical Playwright tests.

# 16 Deployment and rollout

## Environments

| **Environment** | **Purpose**                                 | **Data and credentials**                                                    | **Deployment rule**                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Development     | Local implementation and unit work          | Local or dedicated development services; synthetic data                     | Manual developer start.                                |
| Preview         | Pull-request UI and integration review      | Non-production credentials and isolated database or safe shared test tenant | Automatic from pull request; never production secrets. |
| Staging         | Migration, end-to-end and release rehearsal | Separate Clerk, Neon, Cloudinary and Resend configuration                   | Deploy release candidate after CI passes.              |
| Production      | Approved portfolio MVP                      | Production-scoped secrets and non-sensitive demo workspace                  | Manual promotion after go or no-go review.             |

## Required environment variables

| **Group**   | **Variables**                                                                     |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Application | APP_URL, APP_ENV, SUPPORT_EMAIL                                                   |
| Database    | DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL when required by migration tooling                    |
| Clerk       | NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET |
| Cloudinary  | NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME, CLOUDINARY_API_KEY, CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET      |
| Resend      | RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM                                                        |
| Operations  | INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET, error-monitoring DSN and release identifier                  |

## Deployment sequence

**1\.** Freeze the release candidate and record its Git commit, Prisma migration set and environment configuration revision.

**2\.** Run CI, dependency review, secret scan, type checks, tests and production build.

**3\.** Create or verify a recoverable database backup or branch and record the restore procedure.

**4\.** Apply backward-compatible migrations with prisma migrate deploy and inspect migration logs.

**5\.** Run database smoke queries and constraints before routing users to the new application.

**6\.** Deploy the application to staging, run the primary lifecycle, tenant-isolation and provider contract tests.

**7\.** Promote the same reviewed commit to production and run read-only health checks followed by a synthetic write flow.

**8\.** Monitor errors, latency, webhook processing, outbox age and database health during the release window.

## Rollout checklist

| **Gate**      | **Go criterion**                                      | **Stop criterion**                                                |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scope         | All Must requirements mapped and implemented          | Unapproved feature displaces a Must requirement.                  |
| Security      | Tenant and role tests pass with zero leakage          | Any cross-tenant access or unverifiable webhook.                  |
| Data          | Migration rehearsal and backup evidence complete      | Unbounded lock, failed constraint or untested destructive change. |
| Quality       | Critical unit, integration and end-to-end suites pass | Failure in report, assignment, resolution or closure flow.        |
| Accessibility | No blocking defect in primary mobile and desktop flow | Keyboard, focus or error recovery blocks completion.              |
| Performance   | Approved targets pass in production build             | Target breach without documented acceptance.                      |
| Operations    | Logs, alerts, status checks and rollback owner ready  | No reliable way to detect or reverse failure.                     |

# 17 Rollback runbook

Rollback begins when a release causes tenant exposure, data corruption, failed core lifecycle actions, sustained severe errors or an unsafe migration. Allen owns the MVP decision and records the trigger, time and affected release.

**1\.** Stop promotion and disable the affected write path or place the application in maintenance mode when continued writes could increase damage.

**2\.** Capture the deployment ID, commit, migration names, error samples, affected tenant identifiers and current provider status without copying sensitive content.

**3\.** If the database schema remains backward compatible, roll application traffic back to the last known-good deployment.

**4\.** Restore the previous environment configuration revision when the failure came from configuration. Rotate a secret if exposure is suspected.

**5\.** Do not automatically reverse a migration that dropped or transformed data. Deploy a forward repair or restore into an isolated database, verify counts and obtain explicit go-ahead before replacement.

**6\.** For additive migrations, keep new columns or tables in place while the old application runs. Remove them only in a separately reviewed cleanup release.

**7\.** Pause email and media reconciliation if they could repeat unsafe side effects. Reconcile outbox and DELETE_PENDING records by unique identifier after recovery.

**8\.** Run authentication, tenant-isolation, equipment read, fault read and one synthetic lifecycle smoke test.

**9\.** Resume traffic gradually, monitor for at least one normal operating interval and document root cause and prevention work.

## Rollback verification checklist

| **Area**      | **Verification**                                                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Application   | Known-good commit is serving and critical routes return expected status.             |
| Configuration | Environment revision matches the rollback record; secrets are valid and not exposed. |
| Database      | Schema is compatible, migration table is understood and row-count checks pass.       |
| Identity      | Valid users can sign in; deactivated and cross-tenant users remain denied.           |
| Integrations  | Webhook signatures verify; outbox and media cleanup are paused or safe to resume.    |
| User workflow | Create, review, assign, resolve and close operate without duplicate side effects.    |
| Observability | Error rate and latency return to baseline; no growing queue or webhook backlog.      |

The sequence follows the approved ten-week delivery plan. Technical spikes occur before the dependent feature, and every week ends with a verification gate rather than only a feature demonstration.

| **Week** | **Work package**                                                              | **Dependencies and spikes**  | **Definition of done**                                        |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1        | Repository, environments, design tokens, schema foundation and CI             | SP-01 tenant guard prototype | Build, migrations, typed config and tenant-test harness pass. |
| 2        | Public pages, Clerk authentication, gym onboarding and local identity mapping | SP-02 Clerk reconciliation   | Owner creates one gym; duplicate and webhook replay are safe. |
| 3        | Roles, staff invitations, deactivation and policy matrix                      | SP-01 and SP-02 complete     | All manager and staff authorization tests pass.               |
| 4        | Equipment registry, archive, status intervals and QR labels                   | Core data constraints        | Equipment and QR acceptance tests pass.                       |
| 5        | Fault drafts, signed photo uploads and fault submission                       | SP-05 media cleanup          | Fields and photos resume; one-minute reporting path passes.   |
| 6        | Review, assignment, lifecycle, comments, notifications and email              | SP-03 and SP-04              | End-to-end lifecycle and idempotency tests pass.              |
| 7        | History, downtime, costs, search and filters                                  | Stable lifecycle data        | Fixture totals, pagination and recovery tests pass.           |
| 8        | Manager and staff dashboards and analytics                                    | Indexed history queries      | Metric accuracy and approved performance targets pass.        |
| 9        | Accessibility, responsive behavior, errors, security and edge cases           | Full feature set             | No blocking accessibility or tenant-security defect.          |
| 10       | User testing, fixes, demo data, release and portfolio evidence                | SP-06 restore rehearsal      | Launch checklist passes and known limitations are documented. |
| 11 to 12 | Contingency only                                                              | Explicit scope decision      | Used for defects or delayed Must work, not future features.   |

## Milestone gates

- Foundation gate: schema, tenant guard, identity reconciliation and CI work before feature expansion.
- Workflow gate: fault lifecycle, audit and notifications pass atomicity and concurrency tests.
- Operational gate: dashboard accuracy, observability and failure recovery are demonstrated.
- Launch gate: security, accessibility, migration, rollback and core usability evidence are complete.

# 19 Risks decisions and open questions

## Risk register

| **ID** | **Risk**                                        | **Likelihood**      | **Impact** | **Mitigation and trigger**                                                                 |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| R-01   | Cross-tenant data exposure                      | Low after controls  | Critical   | Central tenant guard, composite constraints and TC-11. Any failure stops release.          |
| R-02   | Clerk and local membership drift                | Medium              | High       | Session authority, idempotent webhooks and reconciliation. Alert on unprocessed event age. |
| R-03   | Users confuse fault and equipment statuses      | Medium              | High       | Distinct labels, transition rules and full-flow usability testing.                         |
| R-04   | Email fails after business commit               | Medium              | Medium     | In-app notification remains; outbox retains deduped retry state.                           |
| R-05   | Draft photo cleanup deletes valid evidence      | Low                 | High       | Explicit media state, parent checks and SP-05 before cleanup.                              |
| R-06   | Concurrent managers overwrite work              | Medium              | Medium     | Version check, transaction and 409 recovery.                                               |
| R-07   | Analytics delays core workflow                  | Medium              | Medium     | Build operational counts first; reduce secondary charts.                                   |
| R-08   | Free or entry plan limits change                | Medium              | Medium     | Verify quotas before launch and keep provider adapters replaceable.                        |
| R-09   | Backup capability does not meet recovery target | Unknown             | High       | SP-06 selects or upgrades plan before production.                                          |
| R-10   | MVP expands beyond ten weeks                    | Medium              | High       | Protect exclusions; contingency only covers incomplete Must work.                          |
| R-11   | Commercial legal and retention gaps             | High without review | High       | Portfolio placeholders only; professional review gates commercial launch.                  |
| R-12   | Limited access to real gym operators            | Medium              | High       | At least five testers and one gym-experienced participant where possible.                  |

## Decision log

| **Decision**                                          | **Status**              | **Notes**                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Modular Next.js monolith                              | Approved                | Best fit for solo ten-week delivery.                                     |
| PostgreSQL and Prisma                                 | Approved                | Relational constraints and transactional workflow.                       |
| Clerk Organizations with local operational references | Approved                | Managed identity; application retains assignment and history references. |
| One gym per user                                      | Approved for MVP        | Schema keeps a future multi-membership migration path.                   |
| Needs triage for new unassigned faults                | Approved recommendation | Dashboard shows Unassigned and Not set explicitly.                       |
| Original staff evidence locks on submission           | Approved                | Corrections are chronological updates.                                   |
| Saved fields and photos                               | Approved                | Draft media uses explicit state and 30-day retention.                    |
| Normal email within one minute                        | Approved                | Failure recovery may exceed one minute.                                  |
| Approved performance and upload targets               | Approved                | Measured under section 13 test context.                                  |

## Open nonblocking items

| **Item**                                     | **When required**              | **Owner or action**                                        |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| FitFix name, product and domain availability | Before public launch           | Allen checks conflicts and changes working name if needed. |
| Commercial retention and deletion policy     | Before commercial launch       | Obtain legal and commercial review.                        |
| Privacy, terms and support content           | Before commercial launch       | Replace placeholders after professional review.            |
| Independent-gym willingness to pay           | Before pricing or billing work | Interview gym operators.                                   |
| Provider plan and quota verification         | Before production launch       | Record selected plan, limits and expected monthly cost.    |
| Backup and restore capability                | Before production launch       | Complete SP-06 and attach rehearsal evidence.              |

No open item blocks implementation of the approved portfolio MVP. The provider-plan and restore items block production launch if the application will hold real operational data.

# 20 Appendices

## Glossary

| **Term**               | **Definition**                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active gym             | The single Clerk organization and local Gym selected for the authenticated user.                        |
| Audit event            | Immutable technical record of a sensitive action, actor, time and entity.                               |
| Equipment status       | Whether equipment is available, limited, out of service or archived.                                    |
| Fault status           | Progress of a repair workflow from Reported through Closed.                                             |
| Idempotency            | The property that a safe retry produces the same logical result without duplication.                    |
| Needs triage           | New report state indicating that assignment and target date are not yet set.                            |
| Optimistic concurrency | Rejecting an update when the record version changed after the client read it.                           |
| Outbox                 | Database record that preserves a required external notification after the business transaction commits. |
| Tenant isolation       | Prevention of one gym reading or changing another gym's data.                                           |

## Sample success and error payloads

| **Case**             | **Example**                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fault created        | { "data": { "reference": "FF-2026-000184", "status": "REPORTED", "triageState": "NEEDS_TRIAGE", "version": 1 }, "requestId": "req_..." }                            |
| Validation error     | { "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Check the highlighted fields", "fieldErrors": { "title": \["Title is required"\] }, "requestId": "req_..." } } |
| Concurrency conflict | { "error": { "code": "STALE_VERSION", "message": "This fault changed after you opened it", "currentVersion": 4, "requestId": "req_..." } }                          |

## Status transition reference

| **From**     | **To**       | **Actor**                    | **Required data**                             |
| ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| None         | REPORTED     | Manager or staff reporter    | Valid report and equipment status selection   |
| REPORTED     | UNDER_REVIEW | Manager                      | Reviewed severity and equipment status        |
| UNDER_REVIEW | ASSIGNED     | Manager                      | Internal or external assignee and target date |
| ASSIGNED     | IN_PROGRESS  | Manager or internal assignee | Optional progress update                      |
| IN_PROGRESS  | RESOLVED     | Internal assignee or manager | Resolution summary                            |
| RESOLVED     | CLOSED       | Manager                      | Verification; cost optional                   |
| RESOLVED     | IN_PROGRESS  | Manager                      | Incomplete-repair reason                      |
| CLOSED       | UNDER_REVIEW | Manager                      | Reopen reason                                 |

## Final implementation readiness statement

This TRD is internally consistent with the approved PRD, maps every material requirement to implementation and verification, records the user-approved decisions and identifies the remaining launch gates. Implementation may begin with week 1 and the tenant-isolation spike. Production launch remains conditional on the security, migration, accessibility, provider-plan and recovery gates defined in this document.
